primary_action.description: Continue EVT Level 2 coursework — month three of ten. This month covers DC fast charging infrastructure, thermal management systems, and regenerative braking diagnostics. I am not skipping a session. The auto sector revenue index is at 79. Unemployment is rising. The robotaxis are multiplying. Every class hour I put in now is a hedge against everything I see happening outside the shop window.
primary_action.expected_outcome: Training progress advances to 30%. High-voltage safety module completed. Battery diagnostics module begun.

secondary_action.description: When Miguel Hernandez reaches out, I take the call. He is younger, he is navigating the same disruption from a different angle — car wash work, automotive-adjacent, trying to figure out where he fits. I do not give him a speech. I tell him what I actually did: I mapped my existing certifications, I found the gap, I enrolled. I tell him about the EVT Level 2 program — cost, schedule, prerequisites. I tell him Patricia approved the shop's contribution. I tell him what the work feels like after a 10-hour day. I do not pretend it is easy. But I also do not pretend the alternative is better.
secondary_action.expected_outcome: Miguel gets concrete, honest information from someone one step ahead of him. Trust between us increases. He may act on it or not — that is his choice.

emotional_state: Tired but clear. The sector data is bad and I know it. But I am not waiting for it to get worse before I act — I already acted. The training is the action. Every day I show up to class is a day I am not just sitting in fear. I still do not know if this works. But I know that doing nothing was not going to work either.
internal_reasoning: The auto sector is contracting. Robotaxi adoption is visible — 7% of people using them regularly is not a rumor anymore, it is a pattern. My shop is still open and I am still employed, but the revenue index at 79 is a warning that my 0.77 role security is being tested. The EV certification path was the right call. Miguel reaching out is a chance to pass something useful forward. I have no financial leverage to offer him, but I have information and I have honesty. That costs me nothing and it might matter to him. Denise Williams is also circling — I will wait and see what she actually wants before committing any energy there.

deferred_actions.description: Watch what Denise Williams actually follows up with. She manages a parking garage — her world is changing too. I am not sure what she wants from me. I will not initiate.
Watch Maria Santos's regulatory push on RoboRide compliance. If the town council puts real friction on autonomous vehicles, that buys time. I am not counting on it, but it matters.
